_doc: Read by gate 2b of the door (`src/mcgyvr/serving/gate-scripts/02-rig.py`). jev-mcorch measures the local replacement for the API-tier agent: a Jev model (src/mcgyvr/decision.py, typed single-token decisions read from top_logprobs) beside a local orchestrator rung, planned in records/plans/jev-mcorch-run-2026-10-03.md. Steps: the engine's logprob fidelity for the product's exact request body on llama.cpp and vLLM, with and without the template's thinking block (0-fidelity); the Jev candidate ladder over the labelled slice on srv1's card 0, llama.cpp (1-jev-ladder); the same ladder on srv2's card, llama.cpp (2-jev-srv2, --host srv2); the in-VRAM candidates on vLLM, AWQ, srv1 card 0 (3-jev-vllm); the orchestrator modes D (schema in context), P (prose delegate, proposer_for) and J (ClassifierProposer, wired by the harness because the CLI does not) per orchestrator candidate (4-orch-modes); and the capacity fill, Jev co-resident with the biggest orchestrator that loads across both cards and host RAM, Jev on srv2 as the alternative placement (5-fill). The labelled slice is derived from records/measurements bench rows by build_slice.py (label = the shipped gate's `passed`); the driver jev_slice.py re-derives every state from the records at run time, so the slice file carries keys and labels only. It drives containers through _jev.sh and the campaign's own drivers and never the serving harness, so it is not held to that harness's markers.
